transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-10-11
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Emma (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Lina (CSM), Jared (Solutions), Aisha (Head of ML, LumenBridge), Tom (VP Eng), Rohit (SRE), Maya (Procurement), Evan (Data Eng)

Summary:
Quick QBR focused on rightsizing Dedicated capacity, locking SLOs for the next quarter, and a pilot plan to validate the proposed changes. Discussed cost tradeoffs with latency, KV/prefix cache, and planned benchmarks. Ended with concrete next steps and owners for the pilot workshop and security attachments.

00:00 - 00:22 Speaker 1 (Emma, Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate y'all squeezing this in. Quick agenda: usage and spikes, rightsizing proposal, SLO alignment, pilot plan, then security/procurement questions.
00:23 - 01:05 Aisha (LumenBridge): Yeah thanks, Emma. Um we've been seeing cost creep across our conversational endpoints since the new recommender rolled out. Want to understand where we can get predictable economics without tanking latency.
01:06 - 01:35 Carlos (Redwood): Sure — we'll walk through per-route breakout, and I have some KV-cache and batch tuning suggestions. Quick callout, some of the terms in our export might show up weird — like mem-cache as "kvcach" sometimes — that's transcription quirks.
01:36 - 02:15 Tom (LumenBridge): Also want to confirm SLA targets for mobile-first use case — our product team is pushing 200ms p50 across US regions, which I know is ambitious.
02:16 - 03:00 Emma (Redwood): Right, so two levers: Dedicated pools (predictable throughput) vs hosted with autoscale policies. For 200ms p50 we recommend a Dedicated baseline with burst lanes. We'll show numbers.
03:01 - 03:40 Evan (LumenBridge): Quick Q — are the burst lanes charged separately, or part of reserved capacity?
03:41 - 04:15 Lina (Redwood CSM): Burst is configurable; you can reserve X capacity and allow Y burst. Billing shows reserved vs burst usage lines. We'll include sample invoice snippet.
04:16 - 05:00 Rohit (LumenBridge SRE): On networking, we'll need VPC peering + private endpoints. We're in AWS us-east-1 and want to keep traffic inside our VPC for compliance. Also KMS integration for the model keys.
05:01 - 05:40 Jared (Redwood Solutions): We support customer-managed KMS and VPC private control plane. There's a short checklist we'll attach.
05:41 - 06:25 Aisha: Ok good. For rightsizing, what data do you need from our side beyond routes and daily TPS?
06:26 - 07:05 Carlos: Route-level QPS, typical prompt length distribution, and peak window samples. If you have 95th percentile sequence lengths we can tune kv cache config and batching.
07:06 - 07:55 Tom: We have rough stats but Evan will pull precise histograms.
07:56 - 08:30 Evan: I can export 30/90 day route histograms; will include tail-latency samples from our APM.
08:31 - 09:15 Emma: Great. Now I'll share our high-level rightsizing idea: shift three low-traffic routes into an M-class instance profile with aggressive quantization, keep the high-fanout session route on a P-class with conservative quantization, and add prefix cache for the recommender.
09:16 - 10:00 Carlos: The quantization tradeoffs — we'll propose 4-bit for the low-traffic; quality delta is minimal for short prompts but we need you to run a small eval set.
10:01 - 10:40 Aisha: We'll run evals, but want guardrails: if hallucination increases we'd rather pay extra.
10:41 - 11:20 Carlos: Totally — plan is staged rollout with canary traffic split and automated rollback if eval scores drop beyond threshold.
11:21 - 12:05 Tom: On the SLO side, what's realistic for p99 and tail? We care about p50 p95 p99.
12:06 - 12:50 Emma: p50 target 200ms is doable with Dedicated. p95 depends on prompt length but we can target <=700ms p95 and keep p99 under 1.2s with proper caching and KV warmup.
12:51 - 13:30 Rohit: Are these numbers measured at the application edge or within Redwood? We need to align measurement definitions.
13:31 - 14:05 Lina: We'll use token-level tracing and include latency breakdown (routing, model compute, network). We'll provide the trace spec so you can map to your APM.
14:06 - 14:55 Aisha: How do we prove costs won't spike unexpectedly during marketing surges?
14:56 - 15:40 Carlos: Two mitigations: pre-warming nodes during known windows, and cap-based autoscale policies with failover to cheaper hosted variants. We can add a circuit-breaker rule.
15:41 - 16:15 Tom: Does failover to hosted affect data residency?
16:16 - 16:55 Jared: It can if hosted region differs; we'll pin to your region or use Private deployment for strict residency. We'll note options in the runbook.
16:56 - 17:35 Evan: On instrumentation, can you emit cost-per-request tags so we can attach to traces?
17:36 - 18:10 Carlos: Yes — token-cost and model-variant tags are part of the SDK; we'll show a sample snippet.
18:11 - 19:00 Maya (Procurement): Logistics: we need a typical contract cadence and the PO template. Also curious about reserved capacity credits and early termination penalties.
19:01 - 19:45 Lina: We'll attach the draft SOW and procurement sheet. Reserved capacity has a stepped credit; we'll outline the typical terms.
19:46 - 20:30 Aisha: Back to rightsizing — what's the expected unit cost drop if we move to your suggested mix?
20:31 - 21:10 Emma: Ballpark numbers: 18-26% token-unit cost reduction on those three routes with 4-bit quantization + prefix caching, assuming current traffic profile. We'll send exact per-route CSV.
21:11 - 22:00 Evan: Nice. I'd like to run a short 48-hour pilot with production traffic mirror — minimal writes, read-only — to validate tail behavior.
22:01 - 22:40 Carlos: Mirror runs are supported; suggest staging with 10% mirror and ramp to 50% then 100% read-only. We'll provide the mirror guide.
22:41 - 23:20 Rohit: For the mirror, do we need separate VPC endpoints?
23:21 - 24:00 Jared: No, you can route mirror traffic over existing VPC peering; we'll show Terraform example for mirrored rule.
24:01 - 24:55 Tom: Who owns rollback during the pilot? Automated or manual?
24:56 - 25:30 Emma: We recommend automated rollback for regressions in core eval metrics, manual for infra incidents. We'll put exact thresholds in the runbook.
25:31 - 26:10 Aisha: What about multi-region failover? If us-east has an outage, do we go to another region?
26:11 - 26:50 Carlos: We have region-failover policies. You can route to a cheaper model variant in a different region; we can keep session affinity to mitigate cold KV cache penalties.
26:51 - 27:30 Evan: Any visible examples for cold-warm cache behavior? I've seen a big p99 spike on cold warm.
27:31 - 28:10 Carlos: We'll share a sample trace showing KV warmup and suggestions to prefetch on session start.
28:11 - 29:00 Maya: Security—SOC 2 and ISO attachments? Our compliance team needs log retention and audit trail details.
29:01 - 29:40 Lina: SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs available. Audit logs retained per account; retention can be extended as an add-on. We'll attach compliance pack.
29:41 - 30:20 Rohit: KMS flow — will keys ever leave our control?
30:21 - 31:00 Jared: Keys are customer-managed; encryption in transit and at rest. HSM integration supported for Private deployments.
31:01 - 31:45 Aisha: Ok, assuming we pilot and metrics look good, timeline to flip routes? Two-phase?
31:46 - 32:20 Emma: Two-phase: pilot (48-72h mirror + canaries), then gradual rollout with 10/25/50/100 traffic steps over 1-2 weeks per route.
32:21 - 33:05 Tom: If we need to pause a rollout, what's the quickest path back to previous baseline?
33:06 - 33:45 Carlos: Instant rollback to prior model snapshot + reroute policy. It takes a few minutes to propagate; we'll test this in the pilot.
33:46 - 34:30 Evan: Does rollback clear the KV cache or do we resume warm state?
34:31 - 35:10 Carlos: Rollback preserves KV if model variants are binary-compatible; otherwise there will be cache misses and a short tail increase. We'll document compatibility matrix.
35:11 - 36:00 Maya: Procurement question — do you require a signed amendment for the add-on retention?
36:01 - 36:40 Lina: Yes, add-ons are appended to SOW. We'll provide templates.
36:41 - 37:20 Aisha: Anything else we should be worried about?
37:21 - 38:05 Emma: Main risks: incorrect prompt length assumptions, unseen spikes, and eval drift. Mitigations are staged rollouts, mirrored pilot, and continuous quality monitors.
38:06 - 38:45 Tom: Speaking of eval drift — how do we alert on quality regressions?
38:46 - 39:25 Carlos: Redwood Optimize can hook to your eval suite and emit regression alerts; we can set thresholds and auto-fence model variants.
39:26 - 40:10 Evan: Will those alerts be Slack/email/Pager?
40:11 - 40:50 Lina: All supported; also webhook to internal incident manager.
40:51 - 41:30 Maya: Do you have an SLA credit table if SLOs aren't met?
41:31 - 42:10 Lina: Yes — we'll include SLA credit terms in the enterprise pack.
42:11 - 43:00 Rohit: For our infra team, can we get the Terraform module example and network ports list?
43:01 - 43:40 Jared: We'll attach a ready-to-run Terraform snippet and a minimal egress/inbound ports checklist.
43:41 - 44:30 Aisha: Great — so to recap: Emma will send per-route cost + rightsizing CSV, Carlos the benchmark guide and KV tuning notes, Jared the Terraform examples and KMS checklist, Lina procurement + compliance docs, Rohit will share spike windows.
44:31 - 45:10 Emma: Correct. Also propose runbook workshop on 2028-10-20; does that work?
45:11 - 45:40 Aisha: Works for us. We'll confirm attendee list.
45:41 - 46:20 Tom: One last thing — competitor angle, we're also exploring Anthropic for a particular gen workload, curious if Redwood can support model mix with Anthropic later.
46:21 - 47:00 Carlos: We can interop via routing policies; not native Anthropic model hosting but routing to external endpoints is possible with consistent instrumentation. We'll put notes.
47:01 - 47:40 Evan: Can we get a quick cost compare vs Anthropic for the same workload?
47:41 - 48:20 Emma: We'll include a apples-to-apples delta in the per-route export but caveat differences in output quality.
48:21 - 49:00 Maya: Procurement timeline: we need PO signoff by end of Oct to start Nov pilot — is that feasible?
49:01 - 49:40 Lina: Yes, if procurement confirms internal approval path this week we can slot you for early November.
49:41 - 50:20 Aisha: Awesome. Any blockers on Redwood side?
50:21 - 51:00 Emma: Only that we need your histograms and APM traces — Evan said he'll provide.
51:01 - 51:45 Evan: I'll drop artifacts into the shared folder by Friday (2028-10-13).
51:46 - 52:30 Jared: We'll also set up a temporary pilot token with limited scope.
52:31 - 53:10 Rohit: For security review, who will own the audit? Is it Redwood or LumenBridge?
53:11 - 53:50 Lina: Redwood provides audit logs; ownership of compliance artifacts remains with LumenBridge but we can support the review.
53:51 - 54:30 Emma: Ok quick recap of owners and due dates — I'll follow up in email and attach the runbook skeleton.
54:31 - 55:15 Aisha: Sounds good, thanks. One last thing—can we get a short note on expected impact to end-user latency during pilot?
55:16 - 55:50 Carlos: Expect minimal changes at p50, small p99 tail bump during warm-up; we'll quantify in the pilot report.
55:51 - 57:00 Emma: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll send materials and lock the workshop.
57:01 - 57:58 Meeting end / off-record chit-chat (untranscribed)

Notes on transcription: occasional word misrecognitions (model, kvcache spelled variably), speaker attribution approximate in places; refer to owners for clarifications.

Recap (as sent in follow-up):
- Immediate: Redwood deliverables (per-route cost CSV, benchmark/runbook artifacts, Terraform examples, compliance pack) due 2028-10-14 to 2028-10-17 window.
- LumenBridge deliverables: route histograms, APM traces, procurement approval path (due 2028-10-18 to 2028-10-21).
- Workshop: 2028-10-20 (2 hours) to finalize pilot runbook and test rollback.

End of transcript.
